## Alternatives considered
### A1. Soft bounds (warnings only)
Rejected. Customer requirement is contractual guardrails; soft bounds do not meet budget-capping and baseline guarantees.

### A2. Predictive overrides reactive (prediction wins)
Rejected. Reactive metrics are required to prevent overload when predictions are wrong; predictive must not force scale-down into saturation.

### A3. Clamp first, then compute predictive/reactive
Rejected. Clamping early hides the platform’s “requested desired” intent and reduces auditability (cannot reason about why latency regressed while max-bound was hit).

### A4. Scale-up uses max(predictive, reactive), scale-down uses reactive only
Not selected as the default. We allow predictive input into scale-down only when it is valid and scale-down safety gates pass; however, the net effect is still conservative due to cooldown and overload blocks.

---

## Consequences
### Positive
- Customers get deterministic, enforceable behavior aligned with contracts.
- Support and SRE can quickly diagnose “we hit max” vs “prediction stale” vs “region shortage.”
- Predictive scaling can improve p95 latency during known ramps while maintaining safety.

### Tradeoffs / risks
- Customers can misconfigure bounds (e.g., min too high), increasing shortage risk.
- Hard max may cap performance during unexpected spikes (intentional by contract); requires clear UX and CS guidance.
- Conservative scale-down may increase cost slightly vs aggressive reactive downscaling.

---

## Rollout and compatibility notes
- Existing Dedicated deployments retain current behavior until the feature flag is enabled.
- On enablement, defaults must preserve behavior unless customer explicitly sets bounds.
- During pilot, require SRE readiness review and alert tuning before expanding to additional accounts.

We need per-account (and ideally per-deployment) enablement with safe defaults, deterministic evaluation, and an ops-friendly kill switch.\n\nGoal\nImplement gating and rollout controls so that:\n1) Existing Dedicated customers see no behavior change until explicitly enabled.\n2) We can enable bounds and predictive mode for select pilot accounts/deployments.\n3) We can disable (rollback) predictive mode quickly if it causes oscillation/latency regressions.\n4) Flag evaluation is deterministic and auditable (what was enabled at decision time).\n\nScope\n- Define flags (names, scope, defaults)\n- Add flag evaluation in the autoscaler decision loop and control plane policy evaluation\n- Add safe rollback mechanisms (global kill switch + per-account disable)\n- Add observability + logging for effective flag state\n- Add admin/operator tooling and runbook notes (minimal for pilot)",

      "ordinal": 1,
      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Feature flag rollout per account/deployment for autoscaling bounds + predictive mode\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-22148-feature-flag-rollout-per-account.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: Autoscaling policies with customer bounds (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)\nTeam: engineering\n\nflags (names, scope, defaults)\n- Add flag evaluation in the autoscaler decision loop and control plane policy evaluation\n- Add safe rollback mechanisms (global kill switch + per-account disable)\n- Add observability + logging for effective flag state\n- Add admin/operator tooling and runbook notes (minimal for pilot)\n\nNon-goals\n- Customer-facing self-serve enablement (Console UX is covered elsewhere)\n- Complex percentage rollouts across all tenants (nice-to-have; start with explicit allowlists)\n\nProposed flags\nA) dedicated.autoscaling_bounds.enabled\n- Scope: account_id, optional deployment_id override\n- Default: false\n- Effect: when false, autoscaler ignores min/max bounds fields (treat as unset) and preserves current platform-driven scaling.\n\nB) dedicated.predictive_autoscaling.enabled\n- Scope: account_id, optional deployment_id override\n- Default: false\n- Effect: when false, autoscaler does not consume forecast inputs; reactive scaling only.\n\nC) dedicated.predictive_autoscaling.kill_switch\n- Scope: global\n- Default: false\n- Effect: when true, predictive mode is forced off regardless of per-account enablement. Used for incident response.\n\nD) dedicated.scaling_policy_api.write_enabled (optional for pilot)\n- Scope: account_id\n- Default: false\n- Effect: when false, updates to scaling policy fields are rejected (or accepted but stored as inert) depending on control plane approach. See notes below.\n\nSemantics / precedence (important)\n- Kill switch (C) wins over everything.\n- For predictive mode:\n  - Predictive is enabled only if (B == true) AND (C == false) AND deployment has predictive_mode configured.\n- For bounds:\n  - Bounds enforcement is enabled only if (A == true) AND deployment has min/max set.\n- Backward compatibility: if flags are false, existing deployments that already have bounds fields (from migrations/backfill) must continue behaving exactly as before; the fields are inert.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Feature flag rollout per account/deployment for autoscaling bounds + predictive mode\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-22148-feature-flag-rollout-per-account.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: Autoscaling policies with customer bounds (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)\nTeam: engineering\n\nhas predictive_mode configured.\n- For bounds:\n  - Bounds enforcement is enabled only if (A == true) AND deployment has min/max set.\n- Backward compatibility: if flags are false, existing deployments that already have bounds fields (from migrations/backfill) must continue behaving exactly as before; the fields are inert.\n\nImplementation plan\n1) Flag source\n- Use Control Plane feature gate service (FeatureGate) as the single source of truth.\n- Provide evaluation by account_id and optional deployment_id.\n- Autoscaler will fetch a signed/effective gate snapshot for each deployment on a TTL (60s) to avoid hot-path network dependency.\n\n2) Data model / API\n- Add \"effective_gates\" to the autoscaler decision context (not persisted long-term).\n- Include a \"gate_snapshot_id\" (hash) in scaling decision audit events so we can correlate incidents to the flag state.\n\n3) Caching + consistency\n- Autoscaler caches flags with:\n  - TTL: 60s\n  - jitter: +/- 10s to avoid herd refresh\n  - hard max age: 5m (after which fail closed to defaults; see Failure modes)\n- Control plane caches can be longer (5m) but must reflect global kill switch within 60s.\n\n4) Failure modes / safe defaults\n- If the feature gate service is unavailable:\n  - Treat gates as disabled (fail closed) for both bounds and predictive mode.\n  - Exception: if bounds were already actively enforced for a deployment and the gate snapshot cannot be refreshed, continue using the last known gate state for up to 5m to avoid flapping; after 5m, log error and fail closed to disabled (reverting to current behavior). (This is a tradeoff; see Risks.)\n- If the kill switch value cannot be fetched, assume kill switch is ON (predictive disabled) but keep bounds gating based on last known state (since bounds are a safety guardrail rather than a risk factor).",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Feature flag rollout per account/deployment for autoscaling bounds + predictive mode\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-22148-feature-flag-rollout-per-account.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: Autoscaling policies with customer bounds (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)\nTeam: engineering\n\nclosed to disabled (reverting to current behavior). (This is a tradeoff; see Risks.)\n- If the kill switch value cannot be fetched, assume kill switch is ON (predictive disabled) but keep bounds gating based on last known state (since bounds are a safety guardrail rather than a risk factor).\n\n5) Rollback mechanisms\n- Global kill switch to disable predictive mode within ~1 minute.\n- Per-account disable for both bounds and predictive.\n- Support tool: internal admin CLI command to print effective flags for account/deployment and last refresh time.\n\n6) Observability\nMetrics:\n- dedicated_autoscaler_gate_refresh_success_total{region}\n- dedicated_autoscaler_gate_refresh_failure_total{region,reason}\n- dedicated_autoscaler_gate_snapshot_age_seconds{region}\n- dedicated_autoscaler_effective_predictive_enabled{account_id,deployment_id,region} (sampled; watch cardinality)\n- dedicated_autoscaler_effective_bounds_enabled{account_id,deployment_id,region} (sampled)\nLogs:\n- Structured log on gate refresh with snapshot_id, scopes matched, cache age.\nAudit:\n- Scaling decision events include: effective_bounds_enabled, effective_predictive_enabled, kill_switch_state, snapshot_id.\n\n7) Testing\n- Unit tests:\n  - precedence ordering (kill switch overrides)\n  - fail closed behavior when gate service errors\n  - per-deployment override takes precedence over account flag\n- Integration tests:\n  - autoscaler loop consumes gates and produces correct bounded_desired behavior only when enabled\n  - kill switch disables predictive even if policy asks for predictive\n\nAcceptance criteria\n- Default OFF for all accounts.\n- Can enable bounds and predictive independently per account.\n- Can override on/off per deployment within an account.\n- Global kill switch disables predictive within <= 60s.\n- Gate evaluation results are visible in logs and included in scaling decision audit events.\n- Failure to fetch gates does not cause crashes; behavior is deterministic and fails closed.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Feature flag rollout per account/deployment for autoscaling bounds + predictive mode\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-22148-feature-flag-rollout-per-account.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: Autoscaling policies with customer bounds (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)\nTeam: engineering\n\nenable bounds and predictive independently per account.\n- Can override on/off per deployment within an account.\n- Global kill switch disables predictive within <= 60s.\n- Gate evaluation results are visible in logs and included in scaling decision audit events.\n- Failure to fetch gates does not cause crashes; behavior is deterministic and fails closed.\n\nRisks / open questions\n- Fail-closed after last-known state expiry could create a sudden behavior change mid-incident (e.g., predictive suddenly disables). Mitigation: keep kill switch explicit for predictive; consider extending last-known for bounds indefinitely since bounds are protective. Need SRE signoff.\n- Cardinality: per-deployment labels can explode. For effective_enabled metrics, we should sample and/or aggregate by account tier; keep detailed per-deployment in logs only.\n- Control plane write gating (flag D): prefer accepting and storing policy fields even when disabled (so pilot can pre-configure), but ensure UI communicates \"not active\". Product/Console alignment required.\n\nReferences / related work\n- Epic: PM-1842\n- Ticket: ENG-22146 (scaling decision audit events)\n- Ticket: ENG-22142 (predictive signal ingestion)\n- GitHub: PR-48263 (account/deployment-scoped feature flags + safe rollbacks)\n\nRollout plan (pilot)\n- Week 1: enable bounds for 1 internal test account + 1 pilot account in us-east.\n- Week 2: enable predictive for the same pilot account with kill switch on standby; monitor oscillation/latency.\n- Expand to 3 pilot accounts if metrics stable.\n\nDone definition\n- Flags implemented, defaults set to OFF.\n- Kill switch implemented and verified in canary.\n- Runbook snippet added to dedicated autoscaler troubleshooting (how to verify/flip gates).\n- Alerts added for gate refresh failures (non-paging during pilot; paging only if combined with scaling SLO violations).\n\n## Comments",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Feature flag rollout per account/deployment for autoscaling bounds + predictive mode\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-22148-feature-flag-rollout-per-account.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: Autoscaling policies with customer bounds (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)\nTeam: engineering\n\n- Flags implemented, defaults set to OFF.\n- Kill switch implemented and verified in canary.\n- Runbook snippet added to dedicated autoscaler troubleshooting (how to verify/flip gates).\n- Alerts added for gate refresh failures (non-paging during pilot; paging only if combined with scaling SLO violations).\n\n## Comments\n\n- 2025-06-13 (Diego Santos): Drafted flag names + precedence. document.title: Feature flag rollout per account/deployment for autoscaling bounds + predictive mode
document.content:
{
  "key": "ENG-22148",
  "team": "engineering",
  "title": "Feature flag rollout per account/deployment for autoscaling bounds + predictive mode",
  "status": "Done",
  "priority": "P0",
  "created_at": "2025-06-11",
  "updated_at": "2025-07-29",
  "creator": "Vanessa Ortiz",
  "assignee": "Diego Santos",
  "project": "Autoscaling policies with customer bounds (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)",
  "cycle": "2025-W26",
  "estimate": "5",
  "due_date": "2025-07-02",
  "labels": [
    "dedicated",
    "autoscaling",
    "feature-flag",
    "rollout",
    "reliability",
    "risk"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-22141",
    "ENG-22140",
    "ENG-22142",
    "ENG-22146"
  ],
  "parent_issue": "PM-1842",
  "sub_issues": [
    "ENG-22153"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "high",
  "release": "dedicated-2025.07",
  "security_review_required": "false",
  "body": "Context
Dedicated autoscaling bounds (min/max) and predictive mode are behavior-changing and must be gated for safe rollout and fast rollback. We need per-account (and ideally per-deployment) enablement with safe defaults, deterministic evaluation, and an ops-friendly kill switch.

Goal
Implement gating and rollout controls so that:
1) Existing Dedicated customers see no behavior change until explicitly enabled.
2) We can enable bounds and predictive mode for select pilot accounts/deployments.
3) We can disable (rollback) predictive mode quickly if it causes oscillation/latency regressions.
4) Flag evaluation is deterministic and auditable (what was enabled at decision time).

Scope
- Define flags (names, scope, defaults)
- Add flag evaluation in the autoscaler decision loop and control plane policy evaluation
- Add safe rollback mechanisms (global kill switch + per-account disable)
- Add observability + logging for effective flag state
- Add admin/operator tooling and runbook notes (minimal for pilot)

Non-goals
- Customer-facing self-serve enablement (Console UX is covered elsewhere)
- Complex percentage rollouts across all tenants (nice-to-have; start with explicit allowlists)

Proposed flags
A) dedicated.autoscaling_bounds.enabled
- Scope: account_id, optional deployment_id override
- Default: false
- Effect: when false, autoscaler ignores min/max bounds fields (treat as unset) and preserves current platform-driven scaling.

B) dedicated.predictive_autoscaling.enabled
- Scope: account_id, optional deployment_id override
- Default: false
- Effect: when false, autoscaler does not consume forecast inputs; reactive scaling only.

C) dedicated.predictive_autoscaling.kill_switch
- Scope: global
- Default: false
- Effect: when true, predictive mode is forced off regardless of per-account enablement. Used for incident response.

D) dedicated.scaling_policy_api.write_enabled (optional for pilot)
- Scope: account_id
- Default: false
- Effect: when false, updates to scaling policy fields are rejected (or accepted but stored as inert) depending on control plane approach. See notes below.

Semantics / precedence (important)
- Kill switch (C) wins over everything.
- For predictive mode:
  - Predictive is enabled only if (B == true) AND (C == false) AND deployment has predictive_mode configured.
- For bounds:
  - Bounds enforcement is enabled only if (A == true) AND deployment has min/max set.
- Backward compatibility: if flags are false, existing deployments that already have bounds fields (from migrations/backfill) must continue behaving exactly as before; the fields are inert.

Implementation plan
1) Flag source
- Use Control Plane feature gate service (FeatureGate) as the single source of truth.
- Provide evaluation by account_id and optional deployment_id.
- Autoscaler will fetch a signed/effective gate snapshot for each deployment on a TTL (60s) to avoid hot-path network dependency.

2) Data model / API
- Add "effective_gates" to the autoscaler decision context (not persisted long-term).
- Include a "gate_snapshot_id" (hash) in scaling decision audit events so we can correlate incidents to the flag state.

3) Caching + consistency
- Autoscaler caches flags with:
  - TTL: 60s
  - jitter: +/- 10s to avoid herd refresh
  - hard max age: 5m (after which fail closed to defaults; see Failure modes)
- Control plane caches can be longer (5m) but must reflect global kill switch within 60s.

4) Failure modes / safe defaults
- If the feature gate service is unavailable:
  - Treat gates as disabled (fail closed) for both bounds and predictive mode.
  - Exception: if bounds were already actively enforced for a deployment and the gate snapshot cannot be refreshed, continue using the last known gate state for up to 5m to avoid flapping; after 5m, log error and fail closed to disabled (reverting to current behavior). (This is a tradeoff; see Risks.)
- If the kill switch value cannot be fetched, assume kill switch is ON (predictive disabled) but keep bounds gating based on last known state (since bounds are a safety guardrail rather than a risk factor).

5) Rollback mechanisms
- Global kill switch to disable predictive mode within ~1 minute.
- Per-account disable for both bounds and predictive.
- Support tool: internal admin CLI command to print effective flags for account/deployment and last refresh time.

6) Observability
Metrics:
- dedicated_autoscaler_gate_refresh_success_total{region}
- dedicated_autoscaler_gate_refresh_failure_total{region,reason}
- dedicated_autoscaler_gate_snapshot_age_seconds{region}
- dedicated_autoscaler_effective_predictive_enabled{account_id,deployment_id,region} (sampled; watch cardinality)
- dedicated_autoscaler_effective_bounds_enabled{account_id,deployment_id,region} (sampled)
Logs:
- Structured log on gate refresh with snapshot_id, scopes matched, cache age.
Audit:
- Scaling decision events include: effective_bounds_enabled, effective_predictive_enabled, kill_switch_state, snapshot_id.

7) Testing
- Unit tests:
  - precedence ordering (kill switch overrides)
  - fail closed behavior when gate service errors
  - per-deployment override takes precedence over account flag
- Integration tests:
  - autoscaler loop consumes gates and produces correct bounded_desired behavior only when enabled
  - kill switch disables predictive even if policy asks for predictive

Acceptance criteria
- Default OFF for all accounts.
- Can enable bounds and predictive independently per account.
- Can override on/off per deployment within an account.
- Global kill switch disables predictive within <= 60s.
- Gate evaluation results are visible in logs and included in scaling decision audit events.
- Failure to fetch gates does not cause crashes; behavior is deterministic and fails closed.

Risks / open questions
- Fail-closed after last-known state expiry could create a sudden behavior change mid-incident (e.g., predictive suddenly disables). Mitigation: keep kill switch explicit for predictive; consider extending last-known for bounds indefinitely since bounds are protective. Need SRE signoff.
- Cardinality: per-deployment labels can explode. For effective_enabled metrics, we should sample and/or aggregate by account tier; keep detailed per-deployment in logs only.
- Control plane write gating (flag D): prefer accepting and storing policy fields even when disabled (so pilot can pre-configure), but ensure UI communicates "not active". Product/Console alignment required.

References / related work
- Epic: PM-1842
- Ticket: ENG-22146 (scaling decision audit events)
- Ticket: ENG-22142 (predictive signal ingestion)
- GitHub: PR-48263 (account/deployment-scoped feature flags + safe rollbacks)

Rollout plan (pilot)
- Week 1: enable bounds for 1 internal test account + 1 pilot account in us-east.
- Week 2: enable predictive for the same pilot account with kill switch on standby; monitor oscillation/latency.
- Expand to 3 pilot accounts if metrics stable.

Done definition
- Flags implemented, defaults set to OFF.
- Kill switch implemented and verified in canary.
- Runbook snippet added to dedicated autoscaler troubleshooting (how to verify/flip gates).
- Alerts added for gate refresh failures (non-paging during pilot; paging only if combined with scaling SLO violations).",
  "comments": [
    "2025-06-13 (Diego Santos): Drafted flag names + precedence. Need confirmation from SRE on failure-mode behavior (last-known snapshot vs fail closed immediately).",
    "2025-06-17 (Rafael Mendes): Prefer fail-closed for predictive immediately if kill switch can’t be fetched; for bounds, last-known is okay since it’s a safety constraint. Please ensure we don’t exceed max even if gates flip unexpectedly.",
    "2025-06-20 (Jordan Lee): Implemented gate snapshot plumbing in autoscaler context; TTL caching with jitter. Added snapshot_id to decision logs; audit event wiring pending ENG-22146.",
    "2025-06-27 (Miles Thornton): Requested explicit global kill switch runbook step and a quick verification query in Grafana to confirm predictive is disabled fleet-wide.",
    "2025-07-03 (Diego Santos): Opened PR-48263 with account+deployment scoped gates and rollback path. Added unit tests for precedence + failure modes.",
    "2025-07-15 (Vanessa Ortiz): During pilot incident review, kill switch worked as expected (predictive disabled <60s). Follow-up: ensure Console shows “predictive forced off by kill switch” reason (tracked separately).",
    "2025-07-29 (Diego Santos): Merged + deployed to canary. Verified defaults OFF for all accounts; validated per-deployment override. Marking Done."
  ],
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "body",
    "comments"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_eef5c665b55d45bcb5e8c799f4f6c039"
}

# Predictive headroom incident investigation

**Investigator:** Priya Shah, Senior Runtime Reliability Engineer  
**Date:** 2026-07-27  
**Task branch:** `task/priya-shah/predictive-headroom-capture-20260727`

## Diagnosis

The predictive autoscaler is configured with a **60-second lookahead**, while the Dedicated predictive-headroom design default is **5 minutes (300 seconds)**. The effective horizon is therefore **240 seconds shorter (80% below the design default)**. This removes most of the intended advance warning for expected ramps and explains why scale-up behaves close to reactive timing.

The incident evidence also shows a compounding controller/allocator mismatch: the controller forecasts over 60 seconds using exponential smoothing (`alpha=0.25`, wall-clock buckets), while the allocator applies a separate **90-second effective smoothing/decay** that trims the surge signal earlier than the controller expects. The combination produces delayed or insufficient capacity even when the controller predicts additional headroom. A one-evaluation-tick burst-credit accounting skew adds allocation churn but is a contributing factor, not the primary lookahead diagnosis.

## Symptom

During predictable/coordinated morning load increases, Dedicated reserved pools do not add capacity early enough. Queueing and allocation rejections rise, followed by latency regression and customer-facing 5xx errors. The incident record reports 6–8% error rates for affected routes across two regions and reproduces the problem with a 3x-baseline, 90-second burst repeated on a three-minute cadence.

## Evidence

1. **Design default and safety envelope — strongest source fetched in full.** The P0 Dedicated headroom-controller design specifies `forecast_horizon` as configurable from 1–30 minutes with a **default of 5 minutes**. The 2026-03-05 PM+SRE design review explicitly agreed on the 5-minute default. It also requires per-tenant floor/ceiling enforcement, a cross-tenant emergency ceiling, a circuit breaker, conservative scale-down, a 5% canary, 72 hours of SLO monitoring, and automated rollback on regression.  
   Source: `dsid_d921e1d4282b45a7b4990e2366bedc05` — `/knowledge/company/sources/linear/business-ops/ENG-62670-workload-forecast-headroom-controller.json`

2. **Observed incident configuration and mechanism.** The incident RCA states that the controller runs a **60-second lookahead** and the allocator applies a separate **90-second effective smoothing/decay**. It directly attributes delayed/insufficient scale-up and reserved-pool shortfalls to the window/decay mismatch, with a one-tick burst-credit skew as an edge condition. Its canary hotfix reduced allocation rejections by 90%.  
   Source: `dsid_fa6744f09ed34014a2cb2c8f2fb979f2` — `/knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-777345-predictive-scale-window-desync-customer-facing.json`

3. **Capacity gates and arbitration.** The accepted ADR requires hard min/max clamps; predictive input only when enabled, fresh, confident, and covered; `max(predictive_desired, reactive_desired)` for scale-up; immediate reactive overload scale-up subject to `max_replicas`; no unsafe scale-down during overload; cooldown/dampening; fallback to reactive for stale/invalid predictions; and decision-linked audit fields (`requested_desired`, `bounded_desired`, bounds, signals, reason codes).  
   Source: `dsid_747bd6fada5d46c7a5021901a98769ba` — `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-autoscaling-bounds-precedence-and-safety-invariants.json`

4. **Safe rollout and rollback controls.** Predictive mode is default-off and requires the account/deployment predictive gate, no global kill switch, and a configured predictive policy. Bounds are independently gated and remain hard when enabled. Gate evaluation is auditable through snapshot IDs. Gate failures fail closed; a global kill switch forces predictive off within 60 seconds. Pilot behavior is explicit allowlisting, per-deployment control, staged expansion, and kill-switch readiness.  
   Source: `dsid_eef5c665b55d45bcb5e8c799f4f6c039` — `/knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-22148-feature-flag-rollout-per-account.json`

## Validation steps

1. Export the affected deployment's effective scaling policy and decision audits. Confirm `forecast_horizon=60s`, identify the config/override owner and timestamp, and compare it with the 300-second design default.
2. Verify effective gates from the audited `gate_snapshot_id`: predictive gate enabled, kill switch off, predictive policy configured, bounds gate state known, and snapshot age below the five-minute hard maximum.
3. Confirm forecasts were fresh, above the confidence threshold, and covered the affected workload. If not, the controller should have emitted predictive-invalid reason codes and fallen back to reactive mode.
4. For the incident interval, graph `predictive_desired`, `reactive_desired`, `requested_desired`, `bounded_desired`, provisioned replicas, `MAX_BOUND_HIT`, `MIN_UNMET`, cooldown reasons, allocator effective headroom, queue depth/wait, allocation rejections, and 5xx rate. Rule out an explicit max bound, placement shortage, stale forecast, or cooldown as the dominant limiter.
5. Replay the recorded pattern (3x baseline for 90s, 1.2x for 10s, then baseline; repeat every three minutes) with identical bounds and allocator settings. Compare 60-second and 300-second horizons in shadow mode. Acceptance: the 300-second policy requests/provisions headroom earlier, materially reduces queueing/rejections, and does not violate bounds or emergency ceilings.
6. Repeat with allocator decay aligned to controller semantics and burst-credit accounting checked on the same evaluation tick. This separates the horizon defect from the allocator and ledger contributors.
7. Canary the 300-second effective horizon on no more than 5% of Dedicated clusters / explicitly allowlisted affected deployments. Observe p95 latency, errors, prediction error, scale actions, cost/replica drift, oscillation, bounds, and circuit-breaker events for 72 hours before expansion.

## Reversible mitigation

1. Set the affected deployment/account's explicit predictive `forecast_horizon` to **300 seconds**, preserving all existing hard min/max bounds, max-step limits, cooldowns, emergency ceiling, and reactive overload override.
2. Apply only through the existing per-account/per-deployment predictive gate. First shadow the decision, then canary to the affected allowlist / at most 5% of clusters.
3. Keep the incident-proven temporary **+15% predictive headroom buffer** and disable allocator aggressive decay in affected regions until the 300-second horizon and aligned allocator semantics pass replay and canary validation. Remove the buffer gradually after stability is demonstrated.
4. Roll back immediately on material latency/error, cost, or oscillation regression by flipping the per-deployment predictive gate off; use the global predictive kill switch if the effect is fleet-wide. Expected rollback propagation is no more than 60 seconds, after which the autoscaler runs reactive-only while hard bounds continue to protect capacity policy.

## Conclusion

The late response is primarily a configuration drift: **60 seconds effective versus the 300-second design default**. The allocator's independent 90-second decay and one-tick burst-credit skew amplify the short horizon. Restore the 300-second horizon through scoped gates, validate against the recorded burst in shadow/canary, retain bounds and the temporary safety buffer, and use the proven kill switch for immediate reversal.
